name: TX-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 partisan lean in a Republican-held seat
Markets price a Democratic win at just 2%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Ellzey: an R+11 district, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage, with prediction markets giving Minton almost no chance. No polls or expert ratings exist to move the forecast, so it stays at a roughly 15-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the race inside single digits, or a major outside-spending surge for Minton, would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Ellzey, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this Republican-leaning North Texas district. The seat carries an R+11 partisan lean, and Ellzey enters the general election with a commanding financial position: he has raised about $4.7 million and holds $2.5 million on hand, while Democrat Danny Minton has raised roughly $44,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are opposing the incumbent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. Prediction markets give Minton only about a 2% chance of an upset. The expected margin is around 15 points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
